seo.title: Plugin catalog — OpenMixer
seo.description: {count} audio plugins tested for OpenMixer on {platforms} platforms: which are accepted, which come with conditions and which are refused, and why.

hero.title: What we measured about each plugin.
hero.lede: Every plugin is loaded, run and measured on a real device before OpenMixer offers it: the audio callback is watched for allocations, locks and system calls, and CPU cost and latency are measured. These are the records of {count} plugins on {platforms} platforms, grouped by what each platform could accept.

accepted.label: Accepted
accepted.meaning: Passed every measurement on this platform and is offered for use.

conditional.label: Accepted with conditions
conditional.meaning: Works, but only in a process of its own. The reason shown is why it is not offered without that condition.

refused.label: Refused
refused.meaning: Not offered on this platform. The reason shown is why.

platforms.title: What each platform accepted.
platforms.lede: The same plugin can pass on one platform and be refused on another, so each platform is counted on its own.

summary.formats: {lv2} LV2 and {clap} CLAP plugins, from {records} records.

list.title: Every plugin, with its reasons.
list.lede: Search the list, narrow it by platform, format, verdict or package, and open a row to read every reason behind it.
list.packagePlaceholder: Package or file, such as lsp-plugins.clap
list.loading: Loading the plugins of this platform.
list.loadFailed: The plugins of this platform could not be loaded.

detail.cpuValue: {pct} of one core, at {rate} Hz and {quantum} frames

reading.title: How a verdict is reached.
reading.one: A plugin is tested once for each way it can be offered. It is accepted when one of those ways passes every measurement, accepted with conditions when the best it can do is to run in a process of its own, and refused when it can be offered in no way.
reading.two: The long-run stability test was not part of these records, so no plugin was judged on it either way.

data.title: Where these figures come from.
data.one: Every figure on this page is read from the qualification records, which are public. The records are pinned to one version, and a script regenerates the page's data from it and checks that nothing differs.
data.schema: The data format and how to refresh it
data.two: A result holds for the file and version shown on the row. If you maintain a plugin and a row is wrong or out of date, each open row links to a form to report it.

reason.hosting_rt-safety_violations-under-notes: While notes were played, in the audio callback: {allocations} allocations, {locks} locks, {syscalls} system calls.

compare.title: Compared with mod-host and jalv
compare.lede: Every plugin of this platform run through each host with the same checks, on one private audio server at {rate} Hz and {quantum} frames: it loads, it gives sound (an effect a tone, an instrument notes), it survives {cycles} load cycles and {soak} seconds of running, and its audio thread is watched for allocations, locks and system calls.
compare.refBetter: {host} does better than omx-clap-host or plugin-hostd on one plugin: {plugins}. | {host} does better than omx-clap-host or plugin-hostd on {count} plugins: {plugins}.
compare.refBetterNone: In this run neither mod-host nor jalv did better than our hosts on any plugin.
compare.oursBetter: {host} does better than mod-host or jalv on one plugin: {plugins}. | {host} does better than mod-host or jalv on {count} plugins: {plugins}.
compare.latencyHidden: {hosts} reports no plugin latency to the audio server, so its latency is not observable.
compare.notObservable: A check a host does not let us observe is shown as not observable and never counted as a failure.

none.no-summary: No comparison with mod-host and jalv has been published for this platform.
none.not-publishable: The comparison run for this platform did not include both mod-host and jalv, so it is not shown.
